requirements.paraphrase: Treat encrypted reasoning and compaction payloads as opaque values.
Never decrypt, interpret, expose, compare across calls, or render opaque provider state as chain of thought.
Keep displayable reasoning summaries separate from opaque continuation state.
Preserve provider-defined item order and adjacency.
Never regroup reasoning, assistant, function-call, function-output, or compaction items by kind.
Make every provider-required item normalization explicit, versioned, and tested.
Bind every provider checkpoint to the exact lane that created it.
Include the complete provider, endpoint, model, configuration, tool, execution, capability, and codec identity in lane bindings.
Reject incompatible continuation instead of falling back to visible-message replay.
Use Avalan-owned public IDs for Avalan logical responses.
Never expose or alias the final upstream response ID as the public response ID.
Keep upstream response IDs private to their provider lanes.
Advance conversation state only at validated execution boundaries.
Never commit a partially parsed streaming item.
Never overwrite a valid parent checkpoint after a failed attempt.
Give store=true and store=false materially distinct documented retention semantics.
Never retain a complete store=false conversation merely to support bare-ID continuation.
Return a typed unsupported-capability error when the selected lane cannot honor requested continuity.
Never degrade implicitly to visible-transcript-only continuation.
Make the coordinator own authorization, binding, request assembly, ordered staging, suspension, compaction, commit, publication, and lifecycle policy.
Keep the coordinator independent of terminal rendering and host-specific behavior.
Represent every required identity, ownership, execution, lane, mode, ledger, compaction, configuration, integrity, lifecycle, and observability concept in checkpoints.
Never conflate the visible transcript with the private provider item ledger.
Create an immutable child checkpoint for every successful logical turn.
Use compare-and-swap or equivalent optimistic concurrency for named heads.
Resolve concurrent advances as explicit branches or one success plus one typed conflict.
Never silently interleave provider item ledgers.
Keep reasoning state within the provider lane that produced it.
Never merge opaque reasoning items from different providers or deployments.
Expose typed conversation mode, parent, reasoning context, inline compaction, standalone compaction, and retention settings.
Return the new checkpoint or conversation handle from every successful result.
Expose the same checkpoint from the terminal streaming result.
Preserve one-shot behavior when conversation settings are omitted.
Require an explicit stored-mode choice and disclose provider-side retention.
Implement stateless continuation with store=false, complete ordered replay state, appended input, and post-validation checkpoint commit.
Use the provider-supported encrypted-reasoning inclusion mechanism when the exact capability profile requires it.
Replay every provider-required output item for all-turns reasoning.
Never treat visible user and assistant text as equivalent to full all-turns replay state.
Do not cache incomplete reasoning items as replayable state.
Fail explicitly when missing provider data prevents requested stateless continuity.
Encrypt stateless checkpoint state at rest.
Authenticate and encrypt caller-held continuation envelopes as opaque tokens.
Implement stored continuation with store=true, private upstream IDs, new-input-only chaining, and provider-managed history.
Do not replay the full prior ledger in stored mode unless the exact provider contract requires it.
Reapply instructions, tools, and generation settings that stored chaining does not inherit.
Disclose that stored continuation enables provider-side retention.
Return a typed terminal condition when stored upstream ancestry expires or is deleted.
Use exactly one continuation mode per provider lane.
Reject every stored/stateless parent-field or lane-binding mixture.
Report opaque-continuity loss when an explicit reset starts a new visible-transcript lane.
Represent auto, current-turn, and all-turns reasoning context as typed choices.
Do not assume every reasoning model supports every reasoning-context value.
Capture the provider-reported effective reasoning context in results and checkpoints.
Retain and replay the full required output sequence for stateless all-turns reasoning.
Send the documented context field and continuation ID for stored all-turns reasoning.
Keep summary selection independent from opaque reasoning retention.
Model inline and standalone compaction as distinct operations with distinct capability bits.
Support the typed provider context-management request for inline compaction.
Validate compact thresholds against the active provider limits.
Do not treat an illustrative threshold as a universal default.
Capture compaction items in streaming and non-streaming responses.
Keep each compaction item opaque and in canonical order.
Record the newest compaction item as the latest checkpoint boundary.
For stateless replay, retain the latest compaction item and suffix while dropping only the provider-authorized prefix.
For stored continuation, advance using the upstream continuation ID.
Never manually prune provider-managed history in stored mode.
Supersede earlier compaction boundaries deterministically.
Expose standalone provider compaction as a first-class operation.
Validate capability and canonical context, call the compact endpoint without tools, and return validated compact output unchanged.
Keep standalone compaction stateless and compatible with zero-data-retention operation.
Commit any optional local checkpoint for standalone compact output atomically.
Leave the parent checkpoint usable after a failed compact operation.
Never label truncation, ordinary summaries, transcript-only retention, reasoning drops, or prompt injection of compact payloads as provider compaction.
Evaluate capabilities at the complete runtime boundary rather than from provider names.
Track stored chaining, stateless replay, reasoning contexts, both compaction modes, stream fidelity, retrieval, and deletion independently.
Use the exact native Azure classifier and bind state to Azure resource and deployment identity.
Account for Azure endpoint, API revision, deployment capabilities, transport parity, retention, and deletion behavior.
Never log or persist sourced live-fixture secrets in test evidence.
Keep generic OpenAI-compatible services incapable by default.
Raise a typed model capability error before provider dispatch whenever possible.
Project unsupported served capabilities as OpenAI-shaped 400 errors with stable Avalan codes.
Never remove an unsupported stateful field and continue silently.
Strictly validate every supported stateful Responses request field and input-item variant.
Reject unknown top-level and nested reasoning or context-management fields.
Default omitted served store to false.
Assign an Avalan-owned public ID to every completed outward response.
Resolve each stored public ID to an authorized immutable checkpoint.
Resolve, authorize, validate, resume, and create a child when previous_response_id is supplied.
Keep stored public responses retrievable for their advertised retention.
Support stored continuation after a fresh server process.
Scope stored response access to tenant and principal.
Delete local checkpoints and follow the documented upstream deletion policy.
Fail store=true explicitly when no durable store is configured.
Do not retain the full store=false conversation beyond its transient processing window.
Do not promise bare public-ID continuation for store=false.
Ensure bounded store=false operational metadata cannot reconstruct conversation or opaque state.
Define a versioned namespaced extension for full-fidelity caller-held served-agent state.
Authenticate, encrypt, bind, limit, and safely reuse the caller-held state extension.
Expose Responses compact at the same configured API prefix as create.
Keep the compact route canonical, authorized, bound, stateless, tool-free, and fail-closed.
Provide authorized retrieve and delete behavior whenever stored Responses compatibility is claimed.
Document deletion, upstream attempts, tombstones, and partial failures.
Never allow a deleted response to remain usable as a parent.
Produce equivalent committed checkpoints for streaming and non-streaming requests.
Stage only complete items, preserve event order, hide opaque data, and publish checkpoints only at valid streaming terminals.
Never retry a logical turn automatically after visible output.
Advance the provider lane at a recoverable boundary before executing requested tools.
Correlate tool outputs and append them in provider order.
Bind pending structured input and provider-lane state to the same execution checkpoint.
Resume durable structured-input resolution from that checkpoint after restart.
Append the human answer after its correlated reserved call.
Advance structured-input continuation state exactly once.
Fail closed for expired, cancelled, declined, or tampered structured-input continuations.
Reuse the durable structured-input continuation contract rather than serializing competing provider state.
Give every child agent an explicit provider lane and ownership relationship.
Never insert one child agent's opaque reasoning state into another lane.
Use versioned, encrypted, authenticated, rotation-capable, bounded, restart-safe durable checkpoints with explicit TTL and deletion.
Authorize lookup, continuation, compact, retrieve, branch, and delete before revealing target existence.
Bind state to tenant, principal, served agent, and deployment without cross-tenant enumeration.
Never log keys, opaque reasoning, envelopes, full ledgers, protected tool output, or storage encryption material.
Document caller-held state as sensitive session material that stays out of logs and URLs and uses authenticated secure transport.
Return stable machine-readable errors for expiry, key rotation, and replay rejection.
Distinguish validation, provider, transport, dispatch ambiguity, visibility, malformed stream, persistence, and publication failure boundaries.
Do not treat an idempotency key as deduplication proof; fence ambiguous dispatch from automatic duplicate continuation.
Do not automatically retry after visible output.
Surface an explicit state-commit failure when a completed provider response cannot be checkpointed.
Never publish a response that falsely promises resumability after checkpoint commit failure.
Define explicit precedence across server, agent, model, request, and provider defaults.
Never let a request broaden retention, provider storage, or capability beyond server policy.
Keep opaque state out of metrics and traces while retaining content-safe operational answers.
Preserve current one-shot model and agent behavior when conversation settings are absent.
Keep the existing tool-call replay path behaviorally correct during migration.
Strictly validate stateful served fields once they are advertised.
Never accept and ignore a stateful OpenAI field.
Reject stored continuation when no durable checkpoint store exists.
Require a proven checkpoint migration or explicit visible-transcript reset after binding changes.
Cover every required unit behavior including integrity, ordering, modes, compaction, binding, authority, limits, validation, errors, and redaction.
Cover every supported provider, mode, transport, execution, turn, reasoning, compaction, lifecycle, interaction, and failure integration combination.
Prove exact provider request shapes for every continuation and compaction mode.
Do not infer reasoning continuity from a plausible final answer.
Prove the complete stored, stateless, authorization, streaming, agent, interaction, compaction, lifecycle, validation, and privacy server flow with the official client.
Verify each activated real provider boundary with bounded live smoke tests when policy and credentials permit.
Never activate a generic compatible provider based on one native live success.
Explain retention, state categories, modes, reasoning context, compaction, continuation IDs, keys, lifecycle, Azure limits, fail-closed compatibility, and safe troubleshooting.
